records.label: Autosomal recessive Stickler family
quotes: Here, we describe the first autosomal recessive Stickler family due to loss of function mutations (c.1176_1198del, p.Gln393Cysfs*25) of COL9A3 gene.

records.label: R08-308A

phenotypes.text: moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss
irregularity of medial distal femoral epiphyses
speech delay attributed to hearing loss

records.segregation: Parents (third cousins) and unaffected sister heterozygous
quotes: In consanguineous Stickler syndrome family R08–308, exome sequencing was used to identify homozygosity for single base duplication c.650dupC in exon 13 of COL9A3 (RefSeq accession number NM_001853.3) of the proband.
Genotyping of the parents and an unaffected sibling showed that all of them were heterozygous for the sequence change (Figure 2).

Femoral and tibial bowing were noted at birth. Radiographs at 6 years demonstrated slightly flattened proximal femoral epiphyses, normal knee epiphyses, and mild platyspondyly (Figure 1). Growth parameters have been in the normal range.

records.label: COL9A3 family (2 patients)
quotes: Six affected patients were identified from four pedigrees with variants in COL9A1 (one family, one patient), COL9A2 (two families, three patients), and COL9A3 (one family, two patients).
All patients were highly myopic with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal, hypoplastic vitreous gel, and all had sensorineural hearing loss.

records.segregation: Variants in trans by parental Sanger sequencing; healthy sibs lacked pathogenic COL9A3 variants
quotes: Targeted sequencing of 166 genes associated with congenital skeletal disorders identified two undescribed heterozygous nucleotide variants in the COL9A3 gene: c.268C>T (p.Arg90Ter) in exon 5, and c.1729C>T (p.Arg577Ter) in exon 30.
Segregation analysis of the identified variants in the family by Sanger sequencing showed their trans‐position.

The clinical features included severe sensorineural hearing loss, high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration, and early-onset arthropathy of the lower limbs. Radiography revealed mild spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia.

records.label: Family 1, II1
quotes: The female proband (II1) from Family 1 is the oldest and only affected individual out of three children from first cousin parents.

She suffers from high myopia in both eyes, in addition to vitreoretinal degeneration with empty vitreous, multiple lattice degenerations and retinal pigmentary changes. There was unilateral absence of the frontal sinus in her skull X-ray. She has severe and progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
The proband in Family 1 was found to have a COL9A3 deletion (c.107_116del, p.(Pro36Argfs*49), rs1470627424), causing a frameshift in exon 2.

records.label: Family 2, II1
quotes: Family 2 presented with two affected individuals out of four children who were born from a first cousin marriage.

Both had a history of multiple vitreoretinal surgeries due to recurrent rhegmatogenous retinal detachments resulting from advanced vitreoretinal degeneration. Despite vitreoretinal surgeries, the older patient is considered blind without light perception (NLP) in either eye
The proband in family 2 disclosed a COL9A3 nonsense variant (c.1204C > T, p.(Arg402*), rs989413835) in exon 23

records.label: Family 2, II2

phenotypes.text: severe visual impairment (counting fingers one eye, no light perception other)

quotes: while his sibling has counting finger vision for one eye while NLP was noted for the other eye. Both suffer from severe and progressive sensorineural hearing loss. Likewise, both show a herniated cervical disc

records.label: Family 3, II1

phenotypes.text: congenital moderate to severe progressive sensorineural hearing impairment
flat acetabular roof with flattened femoral heads

quotes: Family 3 presented with two affected and two healthy children from first cousin parents.

Both affected individuals have myopia and congenital moderate to severe progressive sensorineural hearing impairment. The affected male complains of knee joint pain, especially when he runs. X-ray and detailed examination demonstrated spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia in both children.
the proband in Family 3 showed a one base pair deletion in COL9A3 [c.355delC, p.(Leu119Serfs*9)] in exon 7

records.label: Family 3, II4

phenotypes.text: congenital moderate to severe progressive sensorineural hearing impairment

quotes: Both individuals II1 and II4 have pes planus, depressed nasal bridge and anteverted nares, with midface hypoplasia and downslanting palpebral fissures more pronounced in II4.
None of the individuals showed signs of intellectual disability.

notes.statement: Rad et al. (2022) reviewed patients with biallelic COL9A3 loss-of-function variants and found that moderate-to-profound progressive sensorineural hearing loss and moderate to high myopia with vitreoretinal degeneration were consistent features, while retinal detachment and cataract occurred occasionally and skeletal involvement seemed more variable.
quotes: Consistent clinical features among STL patients with biallelic COL9A3 LOF alleles comprise moderate-to-profound progressive sensorineural hearing loss and moderate high myopia with vitreoretinal degeneration. Retinal detachment and cataract occur occasionally. In contrast, skeletal involvement seems to be more variable.

notes.statement: In 5 patients from 3 unrelated consanguineous Iranian families with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Rad et al. (2022) used exome sequencing to identify 3 different novel homozygous loss-of-function variants in COL9A3, bringing the total number of reported families to 7.
quotes: revealing three different novel, homozygous loss of function (LOF) variants in COL9A3, NM_001853.3.
increasing the total number of families reported to date to seven.

notes.statement: Rad et al. (2022) noted that, unlike Nixon et al. who observed mild Stickler phenotypes in carrier parents, they did not observe mild phenotypes in heterozygous individuals.
quotes: Moreover, Nixon et al. [13] observed that carrier parents can manifest mild STL phenotypes, while our report and others have not observed mild phenotypes in heterozygous individuals.

notes.statement: Markova et al. (2021) compared their patient with 6 previously reported patients from 3 families with homozygous COL9A3 mutations and noted that high myopia and sensorineural hearing loss were uniform, cleft palate was absent in all, and their compound heterozygous patient had a more severe presentation with early-onset arthropathy and vitreoretinal degeneration.
quotes: Congenital high myopia and moderately severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss from a very early age were uniform manifestations for all COL9A3 recessive STL patients, including the one in the present study.
All the described COL9A3 recessive STL cases were characterized by the absence of cleft palate, possibly being a hallmark of autosomal dominant STL forms
Our case further expands the known phenotype with a more severe clinical presentation of an early‐onset arthropathy and vitreoretinal degeneration.

notes.statement: Nixon et al. (2019) found that among 6 patients with recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygous type IX collagen variants, all were highly myopic with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal hypoplastic vitreous gel and all had sensorineural hearing loss; 1 patient had severe arthropathy. They noted that sensorineural hearing loss is more common and severe in recessive than in dominant Stickler syndrome.
quotes: All patients were highly myopic with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal, hypoplastic vitreous gel, and all had sensorineural hearing loss. One patient had severe arthropathy.
Sensorineural hearing loss is more common and severe in recessive SS.

notes.statement: Nixon et al. (2019) suggested that COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 be added to genetic screening panels for patients with congenital hearing loss, as early diagnosis of recessive Stickler syndrome would have high impact for children at risk of dual sensory impairment.
quotes: We suggest that COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 be added to genetic screening panels for patients with congenital hearing loss.

notes.statement: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) predicted that the COL9A3 c.650dupC frameshift mutation causes premature termination of translation and absence of the COL9A3 gene product; the change was not found in public SNP databases.
quotes: The frameshift mutation predicts premature termination of translation and absence of the COL9A3 gene product. The nucleotide change was not found in public SNP databases, suggesting that it was unique to the family.

notes.statement: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that all Stickler syndrome patients with type IX collagen defects had high myopia, midface hypoplasia, and mild to severe hearing loss, whereas vitreous and retinal degeneration had been reported with COL9A1 and COL9A2 mutations but not with COL9A3 mutations. They suggested loss of the alpha-3 chain of type IX collagen produces a phenotype similar to the other type IX collagen recessive forms.
quotes: All of the Stickler syndrome patients with type IX collagen defects have exhibited high myopia, midface hypoplasia, and mild–severe hearing loss. Vitreous and retinal degeneration have been reported in patients with mutations in COL9A1 and COL9A2, but have not been reported in patients with mutations in COL9A3.

notes.statement: Faletra et al. (2014) noted that dominant Stickler syndrome is caused by mutations in COL2A1, COL11A1, and COL11A2, and recessive forms by mutations in COL9A1 and COL9A2. Before their report, only heterozygous COL9A3 mutations had been reported in humans, in association with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 3, susceptibility to intervertebral disc disease, and hearing loss.
quotes: The dominant form is caused by mutations of COL2A1 (STL 1, OMIM 108300), COL11A1 (STL 2, OMIM 604841), and COL11A2 (STL 3, OMIM 184840) genes, while recessive forms have been associated with mutations of COL9A1 (OMIM 120210) and COL9A2 (OMIM 120260) genes.

Up to this time, only heterozygous mutations of COL9A3 gene have been reported in human and related to: (1) multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 3, (2) susceptibility to an intervertebral disc disease, and (3) hearing loss.
